name: RuleRow
intent: One row of an ordered rule list: reorder controls, the caller's condition controls, an optional trailing meta slot, and a delete button. Row order carries meaning in every rule builder we ship — first match wins — so reordering is first-class rather than an afterthought. The component owns the chrome and the affordances; the caller owns the rule shape and supplies whatever controls express it. ```tsx {rules.map((rule, index) => ( {rule.affected} affected} disableMoveUp={index === 0} disableMoveDown={index === rules.length - 1} onMoveUp={() => move(index, -1)} onMoveDown={() => move(index, 1)} onDelete={() => remove(rule.id)} > → every ))} ```.

props.name: children
props.description: The rule's condition controls — selects, inputs, and connective words like "→ every". Laid out in a wrapping flex row, so pass them as plain siblings.

props.name: meta
props.description: Trailing slot, right-aligned before the delete button — e.g. an "N affected" Badge.

props.name: showDragHandle
props.description: Show the drag affordance. Reordering itself is driven by `onMoveUp`/`onMoveDown`.

props.name: disableMoveUp
props.description: Disables the up arrow — pass `true` for the first row.

props.name: disableMoveDown
props.description: Disables the down arrow — pass `true` for the last row.

props.name: ...props
props.description: All standard HTML attributes are supported.
